speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what safeguard can be provided to employers of foreign domestic workers (FDWs) who are required by employment agencies to make advance payment of the FDW's monthly salary purportedly to settle loans or outstanding dues owed by the domestic workers to foreign parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For instance, they may be required to pay their employment agency (EA) a fee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This cost is typically paid by their employers on their behalf in the form of advance salary payments facilitated by the EA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) expects EAs to fully discharge their duties and obligations to employers and FDWs and safeguard the interests of these parties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition to conducting regular inspections, we also act on feedback received and will not hesitate to take irresponsible or errant EAs to task.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is in relation to allocation of risks.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In a situation where an FDW leaves earlier than anticipated, and where a family has already made advance payment to an EA which collects it for a foreign employment agency, could the Ministry consider perhaps the EA issuing a bond such that, if such a situation happens, at least the family can recoup the losses through the exercise of its rights under the bond?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Let the MOM team think through the pros and cons of this suggestion.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At this point in time, allow me to assure Mr Murali Pillai that the employers of FDWs have alternative options and also avenues for recourse.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, although employers generally prefer the advance salary payments because they hope that the FDW will stay with them for the entire contract, there are some employers, who, for various reasons, do not prefer the advance salary payments and these employers can approach EAs that are able to customise a package to suit their needs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, there are varying practices in the market.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For Mr Murali Pillai's point, to protect employers and FDWs, MOM requires the EA to clearly state their refund policies in the service agreement.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, if the FDW terminates the employment prematurely, the employers should check the contract that they signed with the EA, because the contract will lay out whether and under what circumstances they will get a full or partial refund.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Mr Murali Pillai that we take this very seriously.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Every single case that is surfaced to MOM will be followed up and investigated thoroughly.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The suggestion I have made in relation to the provision of a bond is to deal with the function of the EA as a collecting body, as opposed to the usual situation envisaged in a contract where the EA is really seeking to be paid its own fees.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In the context of the EA being a collection agency, perhaps the risks associated with the monies being given to the EA only to be delivered to a foreign EA can be dealt with through the bond system.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member for his supplementary question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: He rightly described it as risk, and a bond instrument could also mean that there will be fee charges which may inadvertently be passed on to the consumer, in this case, the FDW employer.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will also issue warning letters or composition fines to less egregious EAs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The example that Mr Murali Pillai highlighted was that the EAs should not function as a collection agent.
